summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the Tamil redirect Telegram bot. 13/13 pytest cases passed (bot process, no webhook, getMe username, no commands registered, description + short description set, welcome HTML parses without entity errors, keyboard has exactly one button matching env, handler registration order start-before-catchall, MongoDB bot_meta runtime doc present, /api/bot/status returns consistent counts, and direct track() call correctly upserts into bot_events + bot_users). Frontend loaded with no console/page errors; pill='Live · polling', @tamil_best_service_bot, official link matches env URL, all three stat tiles render numeric values (15 / 1 / 15). No real messages were sent to the owner; only read-only Bot API + a controlled sendMessage to chat_id=1 was used to validate HTML parsing.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py still ships unused StatusCheck CRUD (/api/status) leftover from template — safe to remove for a single-purpose bot to reduce surface area.

bot.py uses `os.environ[...]` at import time; if env vars are missing the whole module raises ImportError making the FastAPI /api/bot/status tests harder to debug. Consider fallback + explicit startup log.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral test user 999000111 (TEST_qa_user) inserted then deleted in test_track_and_reply_flow_via_direct_call.
test_credentials: n/a — read-only Telegram Bot API + Mongo direct access
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py covers process/API/DB/keyboard/handler-order. Avoid calling getUpdates or setWebhook (breaks polling). Do NOT DM owner chat 5859128324. Reuse sendMessage-to-chat_id=1 trick for any HTML change verification.
rca_of_the_issue: No issues found. Implementation matches spec: single-purpose long-polling bot, no commands, single inline button, bilingual HTML welcome, analytics + status endpoint working, frontend status card wired correctly.
